related_resources.reason: Definite integration via partition-based finite sums and signed accumulation.
Precise tagged-sum and Darboux definitions and discontinuous examples.
Rigorous limit, differentiation and integration framework.
Foundational real-analysis hypotheses and proof techniques.
MIT 18.100B, lectures 17–18: Riemann integral and integrability.

prerequisites.reason: The construction uses completeness to take upper and lower bounds, boundedness of continuous functions on closed intervals, and convergent-subsequence reasoning to obtain uniform continuity. It does not require differentiation.

recommended.reason: The general compactness and Heine-Cantor statements extend the interval-specific uniform-continuity proof used to make Darboux gaps small.

background: Finite sums, rectangle area, elementary polynomial algebra, and the formula for the sum of the first n integers. No antiderivative or differentiation rule is assumed.
readiness_checks: Can you explain why a bounded nonempty collection of real values has a supremum, even if no value attains it?
Can you distinguish pointwise continuity at an input from one input-distance tolerance that works across an entire interval?
Can you use 1 + ... + n = n(n + 1)/2 to simplify (1 + ... + n)/n^2 and identify its limit?

description: Constructs the Riemann integral from finite partitions and upper and lower sums, explaining why continuity guarantees integrability and how some bounded functions resist integration.
